title: Oxygen Delivery & Cylinders
body:
## Delivery devices

| Device | Flow | Approx FiO2 | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nasal cannula | `1–6 L/min` | `24–44%` | Mild hypoxia, patient talking/eating. Over `4 L/min` dries the nose |
| Simple face mask | `6–10 L/min` | `35–60%` | Needs `6 L/min` minimum to flush CO2 |
| Partial rebreather | `6–10 L/min` | `40–60%` | Reservoir, no one-way valve on bag |
| Nonrebreather (NRB) | `10–15 L/min` | `60–90%` | Severe hypoxia. Inflate the bag before applying; bag must not collapse fully on inhalation |
| Venturi mask | `4–12 L/min` | `24–60%` precise | Titrated COPD oxygen (in-hospital) |
| Blow-by | `6–10 L/min` | variable, roughly `30–40%` | Child who fights a mask |
| BVM + reservoir | `15 L/min` | up to about `100%` | Apnea or inadequate ventilation |
| CPAP | varies by unit | `30–100%` | `5–10 cm H2O` typical start, titrate to `10–15`. CHF/pulmonary edema, COPD, asthma. Needs a spontaneously breathing, awake patient with a systolic over `90` |

## Ventilation rates (AHA 2020/2025)

| Patient | No advanced airway | With advanced airway (during CPR) |
|---|---|---|
| Adult | `30:2`, two breaths in under `10 s` | `1 breath every 6 s` = `10/min` |
| Child / infant, 1 rescuer | `30:2` | `1 breath every 2–3 s` = `20–30/min` |
| Child / infant, 2 rescuers | `15:2` | `1 breath every 2–3 s` = `20–30/min` |
| Neonate | `3:1` with `90` compressions + `30` breaths per minute | same |

Respiratory arrest **with** a pulse: adult `1 breath every 6 s` (`10/min`); child or infant `1 breath every 2–3 s` (`20–30/min`). Each breath over `1 second`, just enough to see chest rise.

> **Trap:** Over-ventilating is the most common BVM error. Fast, forceful breaths raise chest pressure, drop venous return, and inflate the stomach.

## Suction

| Patient | Max per pass |
|---|---|
| Adult | `10–15 s` |
| Child | `10 s` |
| Infant | `5 s` |

Pre-oxygenate first, insert with suction **off**, measure no deeper than the OPA distance, suction on the way out. Vacuum `300 mmHg` or more for adults, reduced for peds. Note: some protocols cap all ages at `10 s` — follow local.

## Airway adjunct sizing

| Adjunct | Measure | Insert |
|---|---|---|
| OPA | Corner of mouth to angle of jaw (or earlobe) | Adult: upside down, rotate `180` degrees. Peds: right side up with a tongue blade. Only in a patient with **no** gag reflex |
| NPA | Tip of nose to earlobe; diameter matches the patient's smallest finger or the nostril | Lubricate with water-soluble gel, bevel toward the septum, right nostril first, straight back not up. Avoid with suspected basilar skull fracture |

## Cylinders

| Size | Constant | Full capacity |
|---|---|---|
| D | `0.16` | about `350 L` |
| E | `0.28` | about `625 L` |
| M | `1.56` | about `3000 L` |
| G | `2.41` | about `5300 L` |
| H / K | `3.14` | about `6900 L` |

`Duration (min) = (gauge pressure − 200) × constant / flow rate`

Safe residual pressure is `200 psi` — change the tank at or before that. Many services swap at `500 psi`; follow protocol. A full cylinder reads about `2000–2200 psi`.

**Example 1** — E cylinder, `2000 psi`, NRB at `15 L/min`:
`(2000 − 200) × 0.28 / 15 = 504 / 15 = 33.6 min` (about `34 min`).

**Example 2** — D cylinder, `1500 psi`, cannula at `6 L/min`:
`(1500 − 200) × 0.16 / 6 = 208 / 6 = 34.7 min` (about `35 min`).

## SpO2 targets

| Patient | Target |
|---|---|
| Normal adult | `94–99%` |
| COPD / chronic CO2 retainer | `88–92%` |
| Post-ROSC | `92–98%`, avoid `100%` |
| Suspected CO poisoning | Pulse ox reads falsely high — give `100%` regardless |

> **Key:** Titrate to a number, not to a device. Oxygen is a drug with a dose.
